tools.name: activity_get-export-csv
tools.description: Streams the activities the activity list would answer for the same filters (the same visibility, deal fence and soft-deleted-parent rules as GET /activities) as CSV, newest first by createdAt then id. Columns: id, type, description, user, contact, deal, timestamp. An export from this endpoint holds at most 100,000 rows AND 50 MB of CSV: more matching rows are refused 413 export_too_large before any row is written (narrow the date range or filters, or export every matching row in the background: POST /account-exports with entities ['activity'] and the same filters as activityFilters). One request streams within a 55 s deadline that also covers the initial count. The LAST line of every response is a trailer: `#conduyt-export,complete,<rows written by the whole export>` when every row was written; `#conduyt-export,continue,<cursor>` when the deadline came: request again with ?cursor=<cursor> and the SAME filters and append that part, which has no header row (the cursor is signed and bound to the account, the filters and the ceiling; any other cursor is a 400 cursor_invalid); `#conduyt-export,too_large,<rows|bytes>` when the ceiling was reached while streaming: discard everything. A response without a trailer was cut: discard it. Optional: contact_id, cursor, deal_id (plus 4 more).

params.name: contact_id
params.description: string (uuid) — only this contact's activities (404 when the contact is not visible).

params.name: cursor
params.description: string — the cursor of a previous part's `#conduyt-export,continue,<cursor>` trailer. Signed by the server and bound to the account, these filters and the ceiling: send it with the SAME filters; any other value is a 400 cursor_invalid.

params.name: deal_id
params.description: string (uuid) — only this deal's activities.

params.name: fromDate
params.description: string (YYYY-MM-DD) — from the start of this day in the account's timezone.

params.name: search
params.description: string — title, description, contact name or deal title contains this text.

params.name: toDate

tools.name: automations_dry-run_automation
tools.description: Dry-run an automation without side effects. Required: id. Optional: mode, source, appointmentId (plus 7 more).

params.name: id
params.description: Resource UUID

params.name: mode
params.description: enum(single|all-paths) — single (default) walks the one path the subject takes; all-paths explores both branches of every condition and marks what it cannot decide as unknown. Any other value is treated as single.

params.name: source
params.description: enum(draft|published) — Which version of the workflow to preview: the working draft (default) or the published one. Any other value is treated as draft.

params.name: appointmentId
params.description: Optional appointment (owned by the contact; calendar.view): the event's appointment for an appointment occurrence, {{extras.*}} tokens and appointment-derived conditions are judged on it. Omitted: the dry run alone infers the contact's latest ACTIVE appointment (scheduled / confirmed, latest start time) for an appointment.booked occurrence and none for any other; the node test never infers one, so an appointment occurrence whose filter reads the appointment is unjudgeable (409) without it

params.name: companyId
params.description: The event's company for a COMPANY occurrence (company.created / updated / stage_changed / deleted / tagged / tag_removed): REQUIRED, 400 without it; needs companies.view, 404 when not found in this account; executionId does not replace it. On any other occurrence it is accepted only when it equals the company carried by the replayed executionId payload, else refused (400). With executionId on a company occurrence it must equal the replayed payload's company (400 otherwise). Company producers carry no contact, so contact filters on such an occurrence are judged as production judges them, without one

params.name: contactId
params.description: Optional contact the simulated event is about: merge tokens, contact-backed trigger filters and contact.* conditions are judged against this real contact (required when the occurrence or the graph reads the contact); refused (400) on a company occurrence, which carries no contact in production (the workflow is simulated without one)

params.name: dealId
params.description: The event's deal for a DEAL occurrence (deal.created / stage_changed / won / lost / ...): REQUIRED, 400 without it (the contact's newest deal is never a substitute); must be a deal you can see (deals.view and pipeline visibility), 404 otherwise; refused (400) when the selected occurrence is not a deal event

params.name: executionId
params.description: Optional id of a stored run of THIS automation to replay (admin or owner only). The replay supplies ONE fact: the company carried by that run's stored payload, read the way the live runner reads it; nothing else about the subject comes from the run. The run must belong to this account and this automation, carry the same trigger event as the occurrence being previewed, and the same contact and deal as the preview; otherwise 404 (not found, or a deal run hidden from API keys without the deals scope) or 400 (other event or other subject). Runs that carry a deal are hidden from API keys without the deals scope. On a COMPANY occurrence companyId stays required and executionId does not replace it (it must equal the replayed payload's company). Omitted, on a non-company occurrence: the preview is a synthetic sample, company rules evaluate as unknown/absent, and the response says so

params.name: previousPipelineId
params.description: For a deal.stage_changed occurrence whose trigger filter reads the pipeline the deal moved FROM: the uuid of that pipeline. Without it such an occurrence is unjudgeable (409). Ignored elsewhere

params.name: previousStageId
params.description: For a deal.stage_changed occurrence whose trigger filter reads the stage the deal moved FROM (from_stage / previousStageId): the uuid of that stage. Without it such an occurrence is unjudgeable (409). Ignored elsewhere

params.name: triggerNodeId
params.description: Optional id of the trigger occurrence to simulate, one of the workflow's admitted occurrences (the column trigger, or a safely placed trigger node of a native v2 graph); omitted: the workflow's default occurrence. An unknown or unadmitted id is a 400

params.name: Idempotency-Key
params.description: Optional: one key per bulk tag operation (1-255 printable ASCII characters, not blank), reused only to retry the SAME request. Same key + same request body replays the original response (Idempotent-Replay: true); same key + a different body is refused with 422 code idempotency_request_conflict (the key is bound to the first request for good: verify it, then use a NEW key). Two DISTINCT 409s under this key, never interchangeable: (1) the ORIGINAL attempt is still being processed (code idempotency_in_progress) — wait for the Retry-After seconds given, then retry with the SAME key; (2) the key was already SPENT by a prior attempt that failed or has an unknown outcome (code idempotency_key_spent) — verify whether that attempt took effect BEFORE sending a brand-new key; resending the SAME key here only replays this 409 again, it never re-runs the request. A third, rare 409 (code idempotency_conflict_retry) means a concurrent claim of this key could not be resolved and nothing was run or stored: retry with the SAME key. If the wrapper's OWN write to RELEASE a failed attempt's claim cannot be confirmed, the SAME key instead answers 503 idempotency_claim_held until the held claim expires — retry with a NEW key, never the same one. If the wrapper's OWN write to confirm a SUCCESSFUL completion cannot be confirmed, the mutation may have gone through anyway: the SAME key instead answers 503 idempotency_outcome_unknown — verify the outcome before any new-key retry, exactly as case (2) above. A blank or malformed key is refused with 400 idempotency_key_invalid, on dry_run requests too (a dry run never records the key).

tools.name: bulk_update-deals
tools.description: Updates up to 100 deals in one request. Each item in `updates` carries the deal `id` plus the fields to change for THAT deal, and each is applied on its own: one item failing never blocks the others. A valid batch of 1 to 100 items answers 200 with a per-item outcome for every item; authentication, billing, request-shape, rate-limit and server failures use their documented top-level statuses instead. Rate limited to 5 requests per minute per account and IP. Length limits count UTF-16 code units as JavaScript does, so a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane such as an emoji counts 2; JSON Schema counts it 1, so a string near the limit can pass this schema and still be refused per item. Required: updates. Returns the new BulkUpdateDealsResponse.

tools.name: calls_link_call-to-contact
tools.description: Board #35, the unknown-caller prompt's 'Search a contact'. Links the call to the contact with a compare-and-set on the locked call row: an unlinked call is linked; a call already linked to THIS contact answers 200 with `alreadyLinked: true` (idempotent); a call linked to another contact is 409 `call_already_linked`, or 404 `call_not_found` when that contact is hidden from the caller. With `attachNumber: true` the call's number (the caller on an inbound call, stored under the account's country) is written into the contact's next free phone slot (the empty primary phone, then phone_2, phone_3 ... the account's numbered phone fields); nothing is ever overwritten, a number the contact already has writes nothing (`alreadyOnContact: true`), every slot taken is 409 `no_free_phone_slot`, and a number another live contact has as its primary phone is 409 `number_on_another_contact` (checked for every attach, serialized per number). A contact erased by a GDPR forget (or being erased) is 409 `contact_forgotten`. With `dryRun: true` the same checks run and the answer says what the request would do, writing nothing. Nothing is written on any refusal. Requires `dialer.create`, plus `contacts.edit` when `attachNumber` is true; the contact must be one the caller may see (404 otherwise) and, for an attach, edit (403 `contact_not_editable` for a collaborator), re-proven under the row lock. API keys need the `calls` scope (a `dialer` key covers it) and the `contacts` scope. A new link records an `unknown_call_linked` activity on the contact and the call's touch. Required: id, contactId. Optional: attachAs, attachNumber (default: false), dryRun (default: false) (plus 1 more). Returns the new LinkCallToContactResponse.

params.name: id
params.description: Resource UUID

params.name: attachAs
params.description: (#632) The one-click 'Add this number' choice; needs attachNumber true. primary = the number becomes the primary phone and the old primary moves to the first empty numbered slot (attached.demotedTo); alternate = the first empty numbered slot. A number the contact already has writes nothing. A full contact is 409 no_free_phone_slot carrying `slots` ([{ slot, number }], every filled slot) unless replaceSlot is sent. A write records a contact_phone_added activity (with the replaced number, if any).

params.name: attachNumber
params.description: Also write the call's number into the contact's next free phone slot.

params.name: contactId
params.description: Contact id

params.name: dryRun
params.description: Run every check and answer what the request would do (attached.slot, alreadyOnContact, alreadyLinked, or the same refusal); nothing is written.

params.name: replaceSlot
params.description: (#632) With attachAs, when every slot is taken: the filled slot to replace. For primary, 'phone' drops the old primary, a numbered slot receives the old primary and drops its own number; for alternate, a numbered slot receives the number (never 'phone'). The dropped number is returned in attached.replaced and written to the activity feed. An empty or unknown slot is 400 replace_slot_invalid. Ignored while a slot is free.

tools.name: chat_get-thread
tools.description: (#684) Only while the workspace's thread view (account setting teamChatThreads) is on; 409 code team_chat_threads_off otherwise. messageId is the thread ROOT (a top-level message; a reply id is a 404). The replies served are the thread's replies that are not deleted, inside the 90-day history window and, for a key whose scopes do not grant deals, not deal cards; total and earlierCount count the same set. Oldest first. Without before: the LATEST limit replies; before=<seq> reads the page below that reply ('Load N earlier replies': send earlierCursor). The root is served whatever its age while it has a reply inside the window (404 once it has none); a deleted root is served as stored (deletedAt set, body 'Message deleted'). aiReactions: an AI teammate's turn that ended with a reaction instead of a reply, computed from its claim (never a stored message), while the reaction stands. replying: the AI teammates whose turn on this thread is running. Both are empty while AI teammates are off. Replies are posted with POST /chat/channels/{id}/messages and parentId. Required: id, messageId. params.name: pointersCursor
params.description: (#613) the pointersCursor of a pointer read that was cut: this request CONTINUES it and answers only the next pointers (data is empty, hasMore false, nextCursor null; no message page is read, no read marker moves). The cursor is syntactic, `<ISO time>_<message id>`, not signed: the interval comes from pointersFrom and pointersTo, which the client sends exactly as the cut answer gave them, and the cursor only says where in it to continue. The server rechecks membership, the deal fences and the retention boundary on every read, so a made-up cursor or interval returns only what the caller may already read. Requires pointersFrom and pointersTo; never with cursor, afterSeq, markRead or readUpTo. Repeat until pointersCursor comes back null: only then is the interval complete. Given once; a value that is not `<ISO time>_<message id>` is a 400.

params.name: pointersFrom
params.description: (#613) an ISO time. On the latest page (no cursor, no afterSeq), `pointers` answers from this time on (never past the retention boundary) instead of only the latest page's time, so a client that holds older pages revalidates every pointer it holds on each poll. With pointersCursor, the start of the interval it continues. Given once; repeated, not an ISO time, after pointersTo, or combined with cursor or afterSeq is a 400.

params.name: pointersTo
params.description: (#613) an ISO time, read only with pointersCursor: the end of the interval it continues (the pointersTo of the cut answer). Given once; repeated, not an ISO time, or without pointersCursor is a 400.

params.name: readUpTo
params.description: Query parameter read by this route.

params.name: topLevel
params.description: (#684, only while the workspace's thread view is on; 409 code team_chat_threads_off otherwise) `true` serves the channel as the thread view shows it, newest first: every top-level message, each with `thread` (its chip summary, null when it has no reply); every reply a person sent with alsoInChannel, at its own seq, with `threadReply` (reason alsoInChannel); and (Paul 2026-11-05) for each top-level message on the page whose FIRST reply was sent by an AI teammate, that reply right after it (newest first: just before it), with `threadReply` (reason aiFirstAnswer). Later replies stay in the thread (GET /chat/channels/{id}/messages/{messageId}/thread). Each reply is still one message: counted once in the chip, unread once, notified once. nextCursor is the last row's id; markRead=true moves the read marker to the highest seq served in `data`. Only the value true; given once; never with afterSeq (the catch-up read serves every message) or pointersCursor. Not given: the answer is unchanged.

tools.name: chat_post-agents-me-mcp
tools.description: (#1140) A stateless MCP server over Streamable HTTP for an AI teammate that runs in the cloud (for example a Grok Bot routine woken by a webhook): it answers JSON only, with no session id and no SSE stream. One JSON-RPC 2.0 message per request; a batch (an array) is refused with -32600. Methods: `initialize` (echoes protocolVersion 2025-06-18 or 2025-03-26, otherwise answers 2025-06-18; capabilities `tools` only), notifications such as `notifications/initialized` (202, no body), `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`. Any other method answers -32601; an unknown tool -32602. Tools (each calls the existing route in-process with the caller's own key, so every rule of that route applies unchanged, the rate limits included): - `reply` {channelId, parentId, body, idempotencyKey, claimToken?}: POST /chat/channels/{id}/messages. Rail mode: idempotencyKey `turn:<messageId>` with no claimToken; the same key returns the first reply (idempotentReplay) instead of posting twice. Claim mode: `reply:<messageId>` plus the claim token completes that claim. - `react` {channelId, messageId, emoji, claimToken?, sourceMessageId?}: POST /chat/channels/{id}/messages/{messageId}/reactions; with a token it ends a claimed turn. - `stay_silent` {messageId, claimToken}: POST /chat/agents/me/inbox/claim with action silent (claim mode only). - `send` {channelId, body}: POST /chat/channels/{id}/messages, a new message (never an answer to a turn). - `linked_record` {channelId}: GET /chat/channels/{id}/linked-record (read-only). - `read_messages` {channelId, limit 1 to 50, default 20}: GET /chat/channels/{id}/messages?limit=. A route's success is the tool result's text content (its `data`); a route's refusal is a result with `isError: true` whose text is the route's error body plus its `status` (for example 409 agent_human_required, 409 reply_stale_claim, 403 Not a member of this channel). Arguments of the wrong type or a missing required argument are `isError: true` with code invalid_arguments, and no route runs. Who: a paired AI teammate key only, sent as `Authorization: Bearer cdy_...` (the chat scope); the same key in X-API-Key, a session, or anything else is 403 agent_key_required. Never put the key in the URL. Mutation budget: this path is NOT charged per request by the key's 500 an hour mutation budget; each WRITE tool call (reply, react, send, stay_silent) is charged once to that same budget instead. Protocol methods and the read tools (read_messages, linked_record) are never charged. A write past the budget is a tool result with isError true: the budget's message, status 429, code mutation_budget_exceeded and retryAfter (seconds). Required: jsonrpc. Optional: error, id, method (plus 2 more).

params.name: error
params.description: A client's JSON-RPC error response (accepted with 202; this server sends no requests)

params.name: id
params.description: A string or a number. Absent on a notification.

params.description: reply / send / react / linked_record / read_messages: the channel id

tools.name: chat_put-agents-me-knowledge
tools.description: (#1209) An AI teammate's listener (by its listenerId, the id its heartbeat and claims carry) reports its KNOWLEDGE FOLDER (a folder on the listener's computer the teammate reads on every turn, whoever asked, read-only; by default the directory the listener was started in). Conduyt stores only, per listener, the folder count, never the path, a file name or contents; every surface reads the aggregate over the listeners whose heartbeat beats now (configured = any of them has a folder; folders = the sum), so a listener started with --no-knowledge never hides another one's folder, and a stopped listener drops out with its last beat. acknowledged: true records that the owner acknowledged the consent on this start ('Anyone who can mention your teammate can ask it about the files in this folder. Set it up for project or document folders, never one holding secrets. Files that look like credentials are skipped, but that is a safety net, not a guarantee.'). The teammate's own paired key only. A report that changes this listener's entry is stored; the audit row ai_knowledge_folder.changed is written when the aggregate changes or on an acknowledgement; a report that changes nothing writes nothing. The teammate's entry is removed when it is revoked. Required: configured, folders, listenerId. Optional: acknowledged. Returns the updated ChatPutAgentsMeKnowledgeResponse.

tools.name: conduyt-auth_start-google-signup
tools.description: The register page's one-click Google sign-up start (a browser flow, before any session; GET on this path is the sign-in start, a redirect). The page sends it on the click, without a terms box; the Terms are accepted on the consent screen after the provider returns. The funnel id and the attribution are sealed into the short-lived httpOnly OAuth state cookie, bound to the CSRF state with a MAC (10 minutes, at most 4 KB); the answer is the Google URL the page navigates to. On the return the callback sends a verified new email to the consent screen (/register/confirm, a one-use pending sign-up of 15 minutes, bound to the browser); accepting the Terms there creates the account, through the same creation as POST /auth/register, and sends the person to the company-name screen (POST /account/company-name). JSON only (415 otherwise), from Conduyt's own pages only (403 otherwise), at most 8192 bytes (413), and a sign-up start budget of 20 per IP per hour, charged only after the body passes (429); the accounts themselves stay capped by the register route's 3 per IP per hour when the consent creates them. Fail-closed when the limiter is unavailable (503). A request with neither Origin nor Sec-Fetch-Site is refused (403). Each start's state is one-use. Optional: attribution, funnelId, termsAccepted. tools.name: contacts_create
tools.description: Creates a new contact. Rate limited to 30 requests per minute. With `callId` (the unknown-caller prompt's 'Create new lead'), the new contact is linked to that contact-less INBOUND call in the SAME transaction: the phone is the call's own caller number (a submitted `phone` must be omitted or strictly the same number, else 422 `phone_not_call_number`), stored under the account's country; `firstName` is required (400 `first_name_required`) and, for this lead only, the account's form-required contact fields and required custom fields are not required (values that are sent are still validated). The caller needs `dialer.create` (an API key also needs the `calls` scope; a `dialer` key covers it). A call that does not exist is 404 `call_not_found`; a call already linked is 409 `call_already_linked` (or 404 `call_not_found` when its contact is hidden from the caller); an outbound call is 422 `call_not_inbound`; a call with no usable caller number is 422 `number_unusable`. The lead's `source` (always 'Inbound Call') and owner are derived from the call, so a request with `callId` must NOT carry `source` or `assignedTo` (any value, null included): it is refused with 422 `call_derived_fields`. Nothing is created on any refusal. callId derives the owner: the call taker, else the signed-in session user; an API-key request, an inactive call taker or an inactive fallback user derive no owner. A contact that derives no owner is then subject to the workspace's normal lead routing and Smart View assignment like any other create, so it may still end up assigned. Optional: Idempotency-Key, dry_run, sandbox (plus 26 more). Returns the new ContactsCreateResponse.

Smart views: `needs_follow_up`, `hot_leads`, `new_this_week`, `recently_won`, `untagged`, `missing_email`, `missing_phone`. The rows never wait for an exact count of a large account: `meta.total` may be null (`meta.total_deferred: true`) or a cached count (`meta.total_age_ms`). `meta.has_more` is always exact; GET /api/v1/contacts/count returns the total of the same filters. A smartListId that is not a uuid is a 400 (invalid_smart_list_id); one that names no Smart List of the account is a 404 (smart_list_not_found). Optional: assigned_to, cf, company (plus 29 more).

params.name: search
params.description: Text search over name, email, phone (any formatting, incl. secondary phones) and company. A Lead ID (8 to 32 hex characters of a contact id or of one of its deals' ids, dashes optional, any case; a whole id matches exactly) resolves by id first: when it holds a hex letter and names a contact you can see, or one owning a deal you can see, the result is those contacts only; when it names none it falls back to the text search. A digits-only Lead ID (also a phone fragment) returns the text and phone matches plus the id matches. With no explicit sort the rows are ranked (exact matches first: the full displayed name, e-mail or phone equal to the term, then a first or last name alone equal to it; then prefix, then other substring; each newest first) and a ranked search serves at most 2000 rows: see meta.ranked_max and meta.truncated.

tools.name: contacts_dnc_get-contact-verdicts
tools.description: Board #32 and #632. Every number the contact owns (the primary, the numbered phone slots, the account's phone-type fields), each with its own Do-Not-Call / litigator verdict (a hold scoped to one number blocks only that number; a contact-wide hold blocks all), and (#632) when a real call last connected on it. `preferred` is the number the dial prefers: the most recently answered number no hold is on (a DNC hold, even an overrideable one, a litigator listing, or any blocking flag), or null when none ever connected or every answered number is held; a dial of the primary takes it, an explicit pick of another number never does (the preference is a pre-call concern: every rep dial goes through this lookup). `requested` answers about the number in `to`, compared country-canonically. The top-level dnc / litigator / suppressions verdict stays PRIMARY-scoped. Requires communications.view or dialer.create; free-text reasons need contacts.view and teammate identities users.view. A contact the caller may not see answers 404. Required: id. Optional: to. Returns the DncGetContactVerdictsResponse.

tools.name: contacts_duplicate-proposals_list-contact
tools.description: The possible-duplicate lines shown on this contact (status open or not_sure), newest first, each naming the other record, plus the email and phone identifiers held from it. Values are never returned: an identifier is a kind (email or phone) and the records that hold it. A record you cannot view is named 'a contact you cannot view' with a null id and createdAt. Both lists are keyset paged, newest first (createdAt desc, id desc): cursor and limit page the proposals (default 50), held_cursor and held_limit page the held identifiers (default 20); a list sent without its cursor answers its first page. total and heldIdentifiersTotal count every line each list shows; nextCursor and heldIdentifiersNextCursor are null on the last page. membershipRevision and heldIdentifiersMembershipRevision are opaque digests of each list's whole shown set, the same on every page while the list is unchanged and moved by any membership change (also one that keeps the total): when a later page answers a revision other than page one's, discard that page and read page one again. Required: id. Optional: cursor, held_cursor, held_limit (default: 20) (plus 1 more). Returns the DuplicateProposalsListContactResponse.

params.name: id
params.description: The contact the line is shown on

params.name: cursor
params.description: The nextCursor of the previous proposals page, unchanged (opaque). Omit it for the first page; an explicitly blank value is refused. A value this list did not issue (a held_cursor included), or cursor repeated with different values, is a 400 code invalid_cursor.

params.name: held_cursor
params.description: The heldIdentifiersNextCursor of the previous held identifiers page, unchanged (opaque). Omit it for the first page; an explicitly blank value is refused. A value this list did not issue (a proposals cursor included), or held_cursor repeated with different values, is a 400 code invalid_cursor.

params.name: held_limit
params.description: Held identifiers per page, integer 1-100 (default 20). A non-integer, 0, a negative value, a value above 100, or held_limit repeated with different values is a 400 naming held_limit.

params.name: limit
params.description: Proposals per page, integer 1-100 (default 50). A non-integer, 0, a negative value, a value above 100, or limit repeated with different values is a 400 naming limit.

tools.name: dashboard_get
tools.description: The counts and totals are cached per server instance for 60 seconds per account, role and visibility scope; for 60 seconds after that a cached copy is still answered while one recompute runs in the background. Under that, every instance shares the last computation of the same account and scope (stored server-side, no person or deal data). A shared copy under 3 minutes old is answered as is, an older one is answered while one recompute runs after the response. Every list with a person or a deal (recent activity, needs follow-up, stale deals, overdue tasks, workload names) is read live on every request. generatedAt says when the counts were read and aggregatesAgeMs how old they were when this response was sent. fresh=1 recomputes now. When the numbers cannot be read in time (another request computing a scope's numbers for the first time, the shared cache unable to coordinate, or this request's own computation out of time) the answer is a retryable 503 dashboard_computing with Retry-After. MCP and CLI parity for this 503 is tracked under board #602. Optional: fresh. Returns the DataEnvelope.

tools.name: deals_update
tools.description: Update a deal. Required: id. Optional: dry_run, sandbox, appointmentAt (plus 22 more). Returns the updated DealsUpdateResponse.

params.name: id
params.description: Resource UUID

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Ask the server to validate without saving; the request IS sent (CLI flag --server-dry-run; the CLI's global --dry-run sends nothing).

params.name: sandbox
params.description: Run the mutation in sandbox mode.

params.name: appointmentAt
params.description: Appointment date/time for THIS deal (ISO 8601 with offset), pushed by the external booking/AI layer. Drives the missed-appointment clock. Send null or '' to clear. An empty string is read as null before validation (it clears the field). Must lie between 2020-01-01T00:00:00.000Z and 5 calendar years from now; a value outside the window is refused.

params.name: assignedTo
params.description: An empty string is read as null before validation (it clears the field).

params.name: checkOrigin
params.description: Pipeline health quick fix: the health check this edit fixes. The body must be exactly that check's fix and `expectedUpdatedAt`: stale = `stageId` (+ optional `expectedStageId`), unassigned = `assignedTo`, missing_close_date = `expectedCloseDate`, missing_contact = `contactId`, each set to a value; anything else is a 400 `health_fix_mismatch` (nothing read or written). A deal at another version is refused with 409 `deal_changed`, one that no longer fails the check with 409 `deal_check_cleared`, both carrying the deal's current health row (HealthFixRefusal).

params.name: closeDate
params.description: A real calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO 8601 date-time; anything else is a 400.

params.name: companyId
params.description: Company id

params.name: contactId
params.description: An empty string is read as null before validation (it clears the field).

params.name: currency
params.description: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. GBP). Omitting it leaves the existing deal currency unchanged.

params.name: customFields
params.description: Patch semantics per key: the keys sent replace those keys (send null to clear one); keys not sent keep their current values, including values written by another writer while this request was in flight. At most 65536 bytes (64 KiB) as UTF-8 JSON (JSON.stringify of the object); a larger object is refused (413).

params.name: expectedCloseDate
params.description: An empty string is read as null before validation (it clears the field). An ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) or date-time; an impossible calendar value or anything else is refused.

params.name: expectedStageId
params.description: The stage the caller's move was chosen against: refused with 409 (nothing written) when the deal is no longer in it.

params.name: expectedUpdatedAt
params.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency pin: the deal's `updatedAt` as the caller last read it. When it no longer matches, the request is refused with 409 `code: 'deal_changed'` and nothing is written. Omit it for last-write-wins per field, except one case refused with 409 `code: 'deal_changed'` even without a pin: the deal's contact changed between the request's first read and its lock on the deal (a concurrent re-link). The pattern above is the server's rule (Zod's ISO date-time check). It also accepts minute precision without seconds (2026-12-01T10:00Z), which an RFC 3339 `format: date-time` validator refuses; send seconds for portability.

params.name: keepPreviousOwnerAsCollaborator
params.description: With assignedTo set to another user: keep the previous owner as a collaborator of the deal's contact (read-only access to the lead and its cards) instead of releasing them. Default false. Cannot be combined with a contactId change. true needs assignedTo set to a user (the new owner) in the same request; otherwise a 400.

params.description: Lost reason

params.name: pipelineId
params.description: Pipeline id

params.name: priority
params.description: Priority

params.name: probability
params.description: Win probability as a 0–1 fraction (e.g. 0.75 = 75%), not a percentage

params.name: products
params.description: Products

params.name: sortOrder
params.description: Kanban column sort position

params.name: source
params.description: Lead source of THIS opportunity (e.g. the campaign/trigger that produced it) — distinct from the contact's first-touch source. Cannot be cleared: every deal keeps a source. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed before the length check, so a blank value is refused.

params.description: Title

params.name: value

tools.name: email_post-opt-out-list-check
tools.description: Answers whether one email address is on this workspace's email opt-out list, and if so its source and since when. It is a POST only so the address travels in the JSON body and never in a URL (request logs keep URLs); it reads and stores nothing. Send a bare address (person@example.com, at most 320 characters). The server is more tolerant than this contract promises, and it also trims, lowercases and strips a display name before matching by hash, so the case of the address does not matter, but only the bare form is documented. Owners, admins and the platform super admin only. An API key reaches it with the emails scope, and a read-tier key may call it (this exact path is the only list route a read-tier key may POST). tools.description: Send an email to a contact. Required: contactId, subject, to. Optional: html, text, replyTo, sendDomainId, dry_run, sandbox. Needs html or text.

params.name: Idempotency-Key

tools.name: emails_create-template
tools.description: Email templates built in the editor keep their builder state in hidden markers: CONDUYT_BLOCKS and CONDUYT_META (subject B, preheader, custom head HTML, footer HTML). Metadata precedence: the CONDUYT_META marker in bodyHtml wins over one in body; the editor writes it to bodyHtml only, and body's marker is read only when bodyHtml has none. A request that would leave DIFFERENT markers in body and bodyHtml is refused with 400 template_meta_conflict ('body and bodyHtml both carry a CONDUYT_META marker and they differ'). Stored rows are never rewritten. Pasted HTML (email only): send bodyMode 'html' with html (your own designed email, up to 100 KB). The stored bodyHtml is built from html: the builder's blocks (from bodyHtml in the request, else the stored row) are kept, and body defaults to the HTML's visible text when none is sent. Sends use the pasted HTML as the body with only what every email gets: merge fields rendered, the preheader / head / footer HTML from the metadata, open tracking, and an unsubscribe link unless the HTML already carries {{unsubscribe_url}} (or {{unsubscribeUrl}}). bodyMode 'blocks' takes the builder's bodyHtml; switching back keeps the pasted HTML (returned as html). Refusals (400, nothing written): html_required (bodyMode html without html, or empty), html_too_large (over 100 KB: Gmail clips emails over 102 KB), html_script (a <script> anywhere in the HTML), html_without_html_mode (html without bodyMode html), invalid_body_mode (not 'blocks' / 'html', or on an SMS template), body_html_required (bodyMode blocks without bodyHtml), body_mode_conflict (bodyMode blocks with html-mode metadata in bodyHtml), html_conditional_comment (an Outlook conditional comment that ends before its <![endif]-->, is never closed, or has an unreadable condition), html_office_markup (VML / Office elements outside an Outlook-only block), html_duplicate_attribute (an element inside an Outlook-only block with the same attribute twice). A template returned by POST, PATCH or GET /emails/templates/{id} carries bodyMode ('blocks' / 'html'; null for SMS) and html (the pasted HTML in html mode, the kept copy in blocks mode, else null); a LIST row carries bodyMode only (fetch the template by id for html). tools.name: imports_create
tools.description: Create an import job. Required: objectType. Optional: ambiguousMatchMode, duplicateCheckFields, fileData (plus 14 more). Returns the new DataEnvelope.

params.name: ambiguousMatchMode
params.description: 'create_new' is retired for new imports (400); use 'proposal' (the default) or 'hold'.

params.name: duplicateCheckFields
params.description: Identity selectors — only 'email' and 'phone' are accepted (case/whitespace-insensitive; any other value is a 400). With removeDuplicates=true they pick the exact-identifier skip fields; otherwise they restrict which identifiers the name-aware matcher may use to recognize an existing contact (a deselected identifier is stored as plain data, never matched on). Empty or omitted = match on both.

params.name: fileData
params.description: Base64 CSV content; at most 25 MB once decoded (413), and it must parse as CSV (400).

params.name: fileName
params.description: Required for CSV imports; optional in JSON mode because the server synthesizes a CSV file name. Must end in .csv (any case: 'A.CSV' is accepted; outside JSON mode); otherwise a 400.

params.name: fileSize
params.description: File size

params.name: fileUrl
params.description: An import file uploaded for this account (POST /imports/upload); not together with fileData or rows; otherwise a 400.

params.name: format
params.description: Set to json to submit inline row objects through rows instead of uploading or referencing a CSV file.

params.name: importMode
params.description: Import mode

params.name: mappings
params.description: CSV column to Conduyt field mapping. Required for CSV imports; synthesized from row keys in JSON mode when omitted.

params.name: metadataFingerprint
params.description: The import wizard's metadata fingerprint. When present, the job is created only if it matches the account's live import metadata, read in the creating transaction (otherwise 409 metadata_changed, no job), and processing re-checks it before the first row (a mismatch fails the job with metadata_changed). Omit it from API calls.

params.name: objectType
params.description: Object type

params.name: reEnrollMode
params.description: Persisted re-enrollment choice for matched (duplicate) contacts. 'additional' re-tags them so they ALSO re-enter this import's campaign while keeping existing enrollments (non-destructive, 'Add to campaign'). 'destructive' cancels their existing enrollments and re-enrolls them fresh ('Move to campaign'). Both require at least one valid import tag (the tag routes to the automation) and are honored across cron/stale/manual resumes.

params.name: removeDuplicates
params.description: Remove duplicates

params.name: rows
params.description: JSON mode only. Row objects whose keys map to Conduyt import fields; nested customFields objects are flattened to customFields.<key> columns. JSON mode: a non-empty array of JSON objects; otherwise a 400. The CSV built from the rows may be at most 25 MB; larger is a 413. JSON mode: the rows must read back as CSV with at least two columns (rows whose objects all carry a single key fail the CSV delimiter detection: a 400).

params.name: smartListId
params.description: Smart list id

params.name: tagIds
params.description: The tags every imported row gets (at most 20; more is a 400). A re-enroll import's campaign tags are among them.

params.name: totalRows
params.description: At most 50000 rows per job (the parsed inline rows, else this declared count); more is a 413.

params.name: verifyLineType
params.description: Opt-in Twilio line-type verification of the imported contacts (tenant-paid, ~$0.008/number). Only honored on a contacts import into an EMPTY smart list; requires the account's lineTypeVerificationEnabled Twilio setting. Verification runs after completion (foreground wizard loop or the verify-line-types cron).

tools.name: me_get-my-email-signature
tools.description: One signature per workspace member. Returns the saved signature (or, when none is saved yet, the draft a first visit starts from: saved false, html null), every field's resolved value and source (fields: profile = the user, workspace = the membership's position and mobile, company = the Company details, signature = department and added networks), and the context the editor previews with (the caller's profile, position, the account's branding and Company details, the caller's own active booking pages). signature.html and signature.plain are RENDERED AT READ TIME from those live sources (exactly what Compose appends on the next send); a profile, membership, branding, Company details or booking page change shows here with no re-save. When the current sources make the saved signature too large to render, html and plain are null and renderError says why. A browser session, or an API key acting as its user (needs the emails scope).

tools.name: me_put-my-email-signature
tools.description: Saving replaces the caller's one signature in this workspace. Every part may be omitted and takes its default: designId classic, overrides {} (every field follows its source), the default options, useInCompose true. Only the choices are stored: the signature is rendered with the public generator's engine from the live sources at every use (this response, GET, and each send). Compose appends it (POST /messages with signature 'new' or 'reply'), rendered at send time, when useInCompose and the matching options.compose flag are on. email is never an override (it is the sign-in address). Links must be web addresses (overrides.web, banner and meeting links) or profile links (social). options.addons.book.pageId must be one of the caller's own active booking pages. tools.name: messages_check-links
tools.description: Checks every link in a draft live from the server, so a dead, redirected, insecure or shortened link is caught before Send. Links are read from the body (and the subject of an email, first) after merge tokens are masked the way POST /messages/check masks them, then from `targets` (whole values, never read as prose); duplicates are collapsed; the answer lists them in the order they appear. Only http and https links are fetched: mailto:, tel: and sms: links are not_fetched; a link with a merge token is merge_field (its address is only known at send time); past 20 web links the rest are not_checked. Safe fetch: a raw IP host, or a host that resolves to any loopback, private, carrier-grade NAT, link-local, unique-local, multicast, reserved or cloud metadata address, is never fetched (blocked_private), and every redirect hop is checked the same way; 5 redirects at most; HEAD first, GET only on 405 or 501 with the body read to 64 KiB at most; 3 s per hop and 8 s per message; a fixed User-Agent, no cookies or credentials. Results are remembered 10 minutes per account and address in the server's memory; nothing is stored and nothing is sent. The answer is notices only: it never changes the Message check score. A `draft` (instead of, or with, `body`) is rendered ON THE SERVER into the message its send delivers, by the send's own functions and with the context the send loads, and the links of that message are checked under the same rules: an email draft (kind compose) as POST /messages delivers it (the inserted template's render with its preheader, custom head CSS and footer, the A/B subjects, the contact's merge fields including custom and date fields, the account and the sender, the sender's saved signature rendered now), or a template editor's unsaved template (templateDraft) as the editor's own Send test (POST /emails/templates/test-send) renders it, with its sample contact and the sender's rep profile; a text-only email is read as the HTML the provider builds from its text; an SMS draft (kind sms) as POST /messages/sms/send delivers it, with the File links block of files already uploaded. The HTML is read as a mail client renders it: what its stylesheets (any selector, in the document or in Outlook-only blocks for the Outlook view) or style attributes hide is not a link. The contact's own unsubscribe link and an uploaded file's link are Conduyt's own (not_fetched). A draft needs communications.create (the send's permission), and each resource it names is loaded through its own endpoint's authorization, for a session and an API key alike: a contactId through contacts.view and the contact's visibility (404 otherwise), a templateId through email_templates.view (403 Missing permission: email_templates.view, as GET /emails/templates/{id}), attached files through files.view and GET /files/{id}/download's record authorization (the parent module's view permission and the parent record's visibility; 404 otherwise), the signature through GET /me/email-signature's rule (an active member; 404 not_a_member); an API key also needs exactly what the send the draft mirrors needs, by the same tier and scope rules as calling it (an email: POST /messages, plus GET /me/email-signature with includeSignature and GET /emails/templates/{id} with templateId; a templateDraft: POST /emails/templates/test-send; an SMS: POST /messages/sms/send, plus GET /files/{id} for each attached file), else 403; a missing or inactive template is a 404 and a corrupt template or a signature too large a 422, as the send. Same access as POST /messages/check (any signed-in member; an API key with the contacts, emails, sms or messages scope, a read-tier key too, when its member may view contacts or email templates). 30 requests per minute per account, a draft included. Budgets: the whole check ends 8 s after the request started: one deadline covers every stage of a draft (its reads, the signature, rendering, parsing, selector matching and the fetches), and a draft not rendered and read by then answers one row (url This message, not_checked, Could not finish the check in time) with truncated true; two drafts are read at once on a server (another answers one not_checked row, Checker busy: try again); a draft's read stops at 200 links (anchors and addresses in the text together), 20,000 HTML nodes, 2,000 stylesheet selectors, 50,000 matched elements of all selectors together and 1 MiB of visible text, and an answer has 200 rows at most: past a cap, the first 199 links, one row (url This message, not_checked, Too large to check fully) and truncated true. A stylesheet selector with :has(), with :nth-child(... of S) or with more than 8 compound selectors is not matched: the read is then truncated the same way (nothing that stylesheet could hide is fetched). The HTML is read in an isolated worker that is stopped at the read deadline (4 s after the start), which then answers the Could not finish the check in time row. A draft's answer carries resourceVersion. Required: channel. Optional: body, draft, subject (plus 2 more). Returns the new MessagesCheckLinksResponse.

params.name: Idempotency-Key
params.description: Optional: one key per message (1-255 printable ASCII characters, not blank), reused only to retry the SAME request. Same key + same request body replays the original response (Idempotent-Replay: true); same key + a different body is refused with 422 code idempotency_request_conflict (the key is bound to the first request for good: verify it, then use a NEW key). Two DISTINCT 409s under this key, never interchangeable: (1) the ORIGINAL attempt is still being processed (code idempotency_in_progress) — wait for the Retry-After seconds given, then retry with the SAME key; (2) the key was already SPENT by a prior attempt that failed or has an unknown outcome (code idempotency_key_spent) — verify whether that attempt took effect BEFORE sending a brand-new key; resending the SAME key here only replays this 409 again, it never re-runs the request. A third, rare 409 (code idempotency_conflict_retry) means a concurrent claim of this key could not be resolved and nothing was run or stored: retry with the SAME key. If the wrapper's OWN write to RELEASE a failed attempt's claim cannot be confirmed, the SAME key instead answers 503 idempotency_claim_held until the held claim expires — retry with a NEW key, never the same one. If the wrapper's OWN write to confirm a SUCCESSFUL completion cannot be confirmed, the mutation may have gone through anyway: the SAME key instead answers 503 idempotency_outcome_unknown — verify the outcome before any new-key retry, exactly as case (2) above. Any executed attempt spends the key, success or not, so a failed attempt usually lands in case (2) above. A blank or malformed key is refused with 400 idempotency_key_invalid, on dry_run requests too (a dry run never records the key).

tools.description: Soft delete: the stage row is kept (so deal history, activities, audit rows and reports keep its name) and the stage disappears from every pipeline and stage list and cannot be moved into; its name may be reused by a new stage. Deleting a stage with no CURRENT deals always works, even if deals once used it (deal history never blocks). params.name: call-dispositions-labels
params.description: Display-label overrides for BUILT-IN dispositions, keyed by canonical value — e.g. {'interested': 'Interested - RFS'}. Only the label changes: the value keeps its side effects, automation triggers and reporting history. Keys are normalized (lowercase, dashes); two spellings of one key are rejected. Labels are 1-40 chars. Overrides for custom outcomes are ignored — set a custom entry's label directly. Keys are normalized (trimmed, lowercased, every run of other characters becomes one dash, edge dashes dropped): a key that normalizes to nothing ('!!!') or two keys that normalize alike ('Foo' and 'foo') are a 422. Keys are trimmed before the length check, so a blank key is refused.

params.name: call-dispositions-status-map
params.description: Disposition → lead status: when an outcome is picked (by a rep or by AI), the contact's masterStatus becomes the mapped value — e.g. {'not-interested': 'lost', 'sale-closed': 'won', 'interested': 'working'}. Keys are disposition values (built-in or one of this account's custom outcomes), values are master statuses (open, won, lost, abandoned, disqualified, or one of this account's custom statuses). Keys are normalized like labels; an unknown disposition or status is a 422. A lead a deal has won is never moved by an outcome. Keys are normalized (trimmed, lowercased, every run of other characters becomes one dash, edge dashes dropped): a key that normalizes to nothing ('!!!') or two keys that normalize alike ('Foo' and 'foo') are a 422. Keys are trimmed before the length check, so a blank key is refused.

params.name: calling-window-acknowledge-any-hour
params.description: Required true when enabled is false: the tenant allows calls at any hour and owns the calling-time rules. Not stored; the change is written to the audit log.

params.name: calling-window-enabled
params.description: false switches the calling-hours check off

params.name: calling-window-end
params.description: HH:MM, 24 hour; must be after start

params.name: calling-window-start
params.description: HH:MM, 24 hour

The save is refused 400 expected_settings_revision_required without it and 409 when it is stale (another save landed first). A contactTableDefaults-only PATCH carries the defaults row's own expectedRevision instead. opId and expectedSettingsRevision are the save envelope: the server reads them before validation and removes them from the body, so the settings schema never sees them (they are not settings and are never stored). A well-formed opId must name a reservation made by POST /api/v1/settings/operations (409 reservation_missing when there is none, 409 reservation_expired past its window); expectedSettingsRevision is required for any change except a contactTableDefaults-only PATCH (400 expected_settings_revision_required) and any other value than the digit string GET /api/v1/settings returned is a 400. Required for every change to the general settings (every key except contactTableDefaults); without it the PATCH is a 400 (expected_settings_revision_required). opId and expectedSettingsRevision are the save envelope: the server reads them before validation and removes them from the body, so the settings schema never sees them and they are never stored.

params.name: opId
params.description: Operation id minted by POST /api/v1/settings/operations (a server-issued reservation). Send it to make the save reconcilable after a lost acknowledgement (GET /api/v1/settings?op=<id>); the PATCH refuses 409 reservation_missing / reservation_expired when the reservation is absent or past its window. opId and expectedSettingsRevision are the save envelope: the server reads them before validation and removes them from the body, so the settings schema never sees them (they are not settings and are never stored). A well-formed opId must name a reservation made by POST /api/v1/settings/operations (409 reservation_missing when there is none, 409 reservation_expired past its window); expectedSettingsRevision is required for any change except a contactTableDefaults-only PATCH (400 expected_settings_revision_required) and any other value than the digit string GET /api/v1/settings returned is a 400. A PATCH that names an opId needs the reservation POST /api/v1/settings/operations made for it; with none stored it is a 409 (reservation_missing). A reservation is good for a short window; a PATCH that reaches the server after it is a 409 (reservation_expired) and nothing is saved. opId and expectedSettingsRevision are the save envelope: the server reads them before validation and removes them from the body, so the settings schema never sees them and they are never stored. An opId with no stored reservation is a 409 (reservation_missing). A reservation past its window is a 409 (reservation_expired) and nothing is saved.

tools.name: sms-providers_get-options
tools.description: Provider picker for the SMS provider dropdown: the id and name of every provider the send service can actually use (active webhook providers whose webhook URL passes the outbound safety check), ordered by name. Reachable with a key scoped `sms` or `messages`; the caller needs communications.view or communications.create. Pagination on this operation is cursor-based and differs from the global `page` / `per_page` rules: - `limit` (1-50, default 50) is how many providers to return. A `limit` above 50 is capped to 50, not rejected; 0, a negative or non-integer value, or a repeated `limit` is a 400. - `cursor` resumes after the last row the previous page scanned. Pass `meta.nextCursor` back unchanged. An empty, malformed or repeated cursor is a 400. - One request checks at most 250 providers, so a page can hold fewer than `limit` items while more remain. Keep paging while `meta.nextCursor` is not null; `meta.truncated` is true exactly when it is set. A 503 with `Retry-After` means the webhook URLs could not be verified right now (a resolver outage); the response is never a partial list. Optional: cursor, limit (default: 50). Returns array of SmsProvidersGetOptionsItem.

params.name: cursor
params.description: string — opaque continuation token: pass the previous page's meta.nextCursor unchanged to resume after the last row it scanned. Omit for the first page; an empty, malformed or repeated cursor is a 400.

params.name: limit
params.description: integer 1-50 (default 50) — how many usable providers to return. A value above 50 is capped to 50 (not rejected); 0, a negative or non-integer value, or a repeated limit is a 400.

tools.name: sms-providers_get-template-options
tools.description: The redacted provider list the SMS Templates page loads: each ACTIVE provider's id, name and colour, ordered by name, for the caller's own account. Nothing else is returned: no webhook URL or headers, field mapping, counts or credentials. The caller needs email_templates.view OR settings.view (the management route GET /sms-providers needs settings.view only). An API key reaches it with an `emails`, `sms`, `messages` or `settings` scope (the member behind the key still needs one of the two permissions). Unlike GET /sms-providers/options (the send picker: usable, URL-safe webhook providers) this lists every active provider, builtin included. Returns array of SmsProvidersGetTemplateOptionsItem.

tools.name: tasks_create
tools.description: Creates a task, optionally on a contact and/or a deal. As a Pipeline health quick fix ('Set next action'), send `checkOrigin` + `expectedDealUpdatedAt` with `dealId`: the task is created only while the deal still needs it (see TaskCreate.checkOrigin); the database allows at most one non-done quick-fix task per deal (a second is refused 409 `deal_has_next_action`). Ordinary tasks are unconstrained: they may coexist with a quick-fix task, and may race one. Required: title. Optional: Idempotency-Key, dry_run, sandbox (plus 9 more). Returns the new DataEnvelope.

params.name: Idempotency-Key
params.description: Optional: one key per creation attempt (1-255 printable ASCII characters, not blank), reused...

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Ask the server to validate without saving; the request IS sent (CLI flag --server-dry-run; the CLI's global --dry-run sends nothing).

params.name: sandbox
params.description: Run the mutation in sandbox mode.

params.name: assignedTo
params.description: A member's user id, `@me` (the caller) or `@owner` (the account owner); null or absent = unassigned (the account's task assignment rules may still assign it). Assigning to someone else needs tasks.assign.

params.name: checkOrigin
params.description: Pipeline health quick fix ('Set next action'): the health check this task fixes. Needs `dealId` and `expectedDealUpdatedAt`. The task is created only while, under the deal's next-action lock, the deal is still at that version (else 409 `deal_changed`), still has no next action, i.e. no open task and no appointment booked from a day ago on (else 409 `deal_has_next_action`), and still fails this check (else 409 `deal_check_cleared`). Send an Idempotency-Key so a retry after a lost response replays the first task.

params.name: contactId
params.description: Contact id

params.name: dealId
params.description: Deal id

params.name: description
params.description: Description

params.name: dueDate
params.description: Any parseable date: a date-only `YYYY-MM-DD` is stored as noon UTC that day; a date-time is stored as given. An ISO 8601 date or date-time the runtime can parse; anything else is refused with `Invalid dueDate`.

params.name: expectedDealUpdatedAt
params.description: With `checkOrigin` only: the deal's `updatedAt` as the health row carried it (PipelineHealthDeal.updatedAt). The pattern above is the server's rule (Zod's ISO date-time check). It also accepts minute precision without seconds (2026-12-01T10:00Z), which an RFC 3339 `format: date-time` validator refuses; send seconds for portability.

tools.name: webhooks_inbound-form-submission
tools.description: Public: no API key; the token in the URL is the credential (create one with POST /integrations/wordpress-forms/intakes). For Gravity Forms (Webhooks Add-On), WPForms (Webhooks addon) and Elementor Pro (Webhook action). Accepts JSON, application/x-www-form-urlencoded (Elementor's default and 'Advanced Data' bracket forms) and multipart without files, up to 64 KB. Field names match case-insensitively with spaces and punctuation ignored: first name (firstName, first_name, first, 'First Name'), last name, a single name / full_name / 'Your name' (split on the first space), email ('E-mail', 'Email Address'), phone (tel, telephone, 'Phone Number'), company, message (comments, notes), utm_source / utm_medium / utm_campaign / utm_term / utm_content, 'Page URL' and 'Page Title' (attribution), tags (an array or a comma-separated string), source, form_name (names the timeline entry). Elementor's form_id, Date, Time, User Agent, Remote IP and Powered by are dropped. Any other field is saved to the contact custom field whose key or label matches it; every field is on the contact's timeline entry 'Submitted <form name>'. Creates or updates the contact by email then phone (a resend never creates a second contact or a second timeline entry) and applies the intake's default tag, source and owner (explicit source / tags in the body win). Required: token. Optional: Page_Title, Page_URL, company (plus 14 more). Returns the new WebhooksInboundFormSubmissionResponse. (public)

tools.name: webhooks_replay
tools.description: Re-enqueues up to 100 matching deliveries (oldest first). At least one of deliveryIds, eventType or status is required. With no status, only failed deliveries are selected. Replaying succeeded deliveries requires forceSucceededReplay with confirmSucceededReplay REPLAY_SUCCEEDED. Settlement-unconfirmed deliveries (dispatched: the request left and no outcome was recorded; unconfirmed: the stale sweep's terminal form of the same ambiguity) may already have been accepted by the receiver: they are selected only with forceDispatchedReplay and confirmDispatchedReplay REPLAY_DISPATCHED, which states the receiver was checked and did not get them. Manual test deliveries are never replayed. A consent delivery (contact.sms_number_opt_in / opt_out) is replayed only while its consent event is still the latest for the number; one superseded by a newer consent event is refused (consentOrderSupersededIds), so a replay can never reverse the subscriber's current consent state. Optional: confirmAmbiguousSmsReplay, confirmDispatchedReplay, confirmSucceededReplay (plus 8 more). Returns the new WebhooksReplayResponse.

params.name: confirmAmbiguousSmsReplay
params.description: Must be REPLAY_AMBIGUOUS_SMS when forceAmbiguousSmsReplay is true.

params.name: confirmDispatchedReplay
params.description: Must be REPLAY_DISPATCHED when forceDispatchedReplay is true, confirming the receiver was checked and did not get them.

params.name: confirmSucceededReplay
params.description: Must be REPLAY_SUCCEEDED when forceSucceededReplay is true.

params.name: deliveryIds
params.description: Delivery ids

params.name: eventType
params.description: Event type

params.name: forceAmbiguousSmsReplay
params.description: Legacy webhook log ids only; re-fires parked ambiguous drip SMS rows. Requires confirmAmbiguousSmsReplay: 'REPLAY_AMBIGUOUS_SMS'; otherwise a 400.

params.name: forceDispatchedReplay
params.description: Also selects settlement-unconfirmed (dispatched, unconfirmed) deliveries. Requires confirmDispatchedReplay: 'REPLAY_DISPATCHED'; otherwise a 400.

params.name: forceSucceededReplay
params.description: Requires confirmSucceededReplay: 'REPLAY_SUCCEEDED'; otherwise a 400.

params.name: fromDate
params.description: The pattern above is the server's rule (Zod's ISO date-time check). It also accepts minute precision without seconds (2026-12-01T10:00Z), which an RFC 3339 `format: date-time` validator refuses; send seconds for portability.

params.name: status
params.description: dispatched and unconfirmed require forceDispatchedReplay with confirmDispatchedReplay. dispatched and unconfirmed need forceDispatchedReplay: true with confirmDispatchedReplay: 'REPLAY_DISPATCHED'; otherwise a 400.

params.name: toDate
params.description: The pattern above is the server's rule (Zod's ISO date-time check). It also accepts minute precision without seconds (2026-12-01T10:00Z), which an RFC 3339 `format: date-time` validator refuses; send seconds for portability.

tools.name: contacts_duplicate-proposals_post-contacts-id-proposal-id
tools.description: Deprecated alias of contacts_duplicate-proposals_decide-contact (renamed in the proposals look release; kept so existing callers keep working, same guards). Record a decision on one possible-duplicate pair shown on contact id (identity rules v2; contacts:edit on BOTH records). decision is required and exactly one of: not_sure (keep both records visible, the pair stays listed), different (different people: never shown again, FINAL), merge (record that the pair is ALREADY merged; this never merges: merge first with the contacts merge endpoint, else 409 not_merged). Other refusals: 409 already_decided, 403 other_record_not_editable, 404, 400. Answers { id, status, decidedAt, previousMembershipRevision, membershipRevision, total }: membershipRevision and total are the contact's proposals list AFTER the decision, previousMembershipRevision the digest just BEFORE it (equal on an idempotent repeat); keep loaded pages only when previousMembershipRevision equals the revision you hold. Required: id, proposalId, decision. Returns the new DuplicateProposalsDecideContactResponse.

params.name: id
params.description: The contact the line is shown on

params.name: proposalId
params.description: The possible-duplicate line (from GET /contacts/{id}/duplicate-proposals)

params.name: decision
params.description: not_sure | different | merge (merge only records a pair that is already merged)

tools.name: contacts_duplicate-proposals_get-contacts-id
tools.description: Deprecated alias of contacts_duplicate-proposals_list-contact (renamed in the proposals look release; kept so existing callers keep working, same guards). List the possible duplicates of contact id (identity rules v2, read-only, contacts:view): { proposals, heldIdentifiers, total, nextCursor, membershipRevision, heldIdentifiersTotal, heldIdentifiersNextCursor, heldIdentifiersMembershipRevision }. Each proposal has id (the proposalId for contacts_duplicate-proposals_decide-contact), status (open | not_sure), rule, raisedHere and other { id, name, createdAt, visible, editable }; a record you cannot view is 'a contact you cannot view' with no id. heldIdentifiers are emails or phones held from this record because another record owns them (value-free). Both lists are keyset paged, newest first: cursor / limit (1-100, default 50) page the proposals, held_cursor / held_limit (1-100, default 20) the held identifiers; pass nextCursor / heldIdentifiersNextCursor back unchanged (null on the last page). membershipRevision and heldIdentifiersMembershipRevision are opaque digests of each list: when a later page answers another revision than page one, discard it and read page one again. 400 invalid_cursor for a cursor this list did not issue. Required: id. Optional: cursor, limit, held_cursor, held_limit. Returns the DuplicateProposalsListContactResponse.

params.name: id
params.description: The contact the line is shown on

params.name: cursor
params.description: The nextCursor of the previous proposals page, unchanged (opaque). Omit it for the first page; an explicitly blank value is refused. A value this list did not issue (a held_cursor included), or cursor repeated with different values, is a 400 code invalid_cursor.

params.name: held_cursor
params.description: The heldIdentifiersNextCursor of the previous held identifiers page, unchanged (opaque). Omit it for the first page; an explicitly blank value is refused. A value this list did not issue (a proposals cursor included), or held_cursor repeated with different values, is a 400 code invalid_cursor.

params.name: held_limit
params.description: Held identifiers per page, integer 1-100 (default 20). A non-integer, 0, a negative value, a value above 100, or held_limit repeated with different values is a 400 naming held_limit.

params.name: limit
params.description: Proposals per page, integer 1-100 (default 50). A non-integer, 0, a negative value, a value above 100, or limit repeated with different values is a 400 naming limit.
